messages:
devon: Alert: getting a flood of 502s from edge-proxy us-east-1. CloudWatch shows NAT gateway port usage at ~94% and steady increase. Affects model-pull + external API calls. Noticing lat spikes on dedicated pools.

sre-bot: [ALERT] natgw-ephemeral-capacity-high - us-east-1 - 94% ports used - 502 spike detected (auto-opened).

ajones: On it. Is this across all AZs or concentrated in a subset? Any recent deploys touching connection handling?

devon: Looks concentrated to subnets in us-east-1a (edge-proxy autoscaled there). No app-level deploys in last 3 hours. We did flip a routing change earlier for a canary, but shouldn't affect egress.

maria-g: Quick grab from one edge-proxy host netstat (lots of TIME_WAIT):
```
tcp 0 0 10.0.4.12:34512 54.239.28.85:443 TIME_WAIT
tcp 0 0 10.0.4.12:34514 52.94.76.12:443 TIME_WAIT
... (~12k lines of TIME_WAIT)
```

kevin: Root cause looks like ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT gateways (NAT IPs hitting port ceiling). Options: add more NAT gateways (new EIP per gw), create an internal HTTP pooling proxy, or route traffic through a different AZ.

tina: I can spin up an extra NAT gateway in us-east-1a and update the route table for affected subnets. Do we want an immediate change or prefer shifting subnets to us-east-1b temporarily?

devon: Immediate help: add another NAT gw in the same AZ and attach to the route table for the worker subnets. Also reduce model-pull fanout if possible. Longer-term: enable http keepalive/connection reuse in edge-proxy.

ajones: Doing NAT gw add now. Also checking if edge-proxy disables keepalive by default (I think 1.14.0 does). If so, enable keepalive in the next hotfix.

monitoring-bot: Created incident INC-2028-457 - natgw-port-exhaustion - pagerduty notified.

kevin: Note: changing ephemeral port ranges on hosts only helps NAT instances. For AWS-managed NAT Gateway the limit is per elastic IP pair; you need additional NAT gw/EIPs to get more ports.

maria-g: After adding a second NAT gw and updating the route table, port usage dropped to ~56% within 90s and 502s subsided. Still seeing micro-spikes when model pulls burst.

devon: Good. Prioritize a 1.14.1 edge-proxy patch to enable keepalive + connection pooling. Also add an internal proxy (egress-proxy) that multiplexes outbound connections for model pulls. This will reduce port churn long-term.

ajones: I'll document immediate steps in the incident runbook and schedule the hotfix rollout. Plan: (1) hotfix keepalive to canary, (2) provision egress-proxy in us-east-1, (3) autoscale NAT gw capacity via infra playbook.

kevin: Another follow-up: evaluate sharding model pulls by region and add backpressure in the model-store clients to avoid large simultaneous cold pulls.

maria-g: Postmortem todo: identify which client/library opens new TLS for every request. We found a few legacy clients with keepalive disabled.

devon: Thanks all — short term mitigated, tracking follow-ups. I'll drop a summary in #incidents and assign owners for the fix. :thumbsup:
